messages:
Maeve: quick handoff — night bridge summary for EU routing blip. TL;DR: routing-rule deploy accidentally narrowed eligible backends, PD filter prevented primary from paging, some customers in eu-west experienced intermittent 503s from 02:12–02:45 UTC. rollback and hot-pool failover done; traffic stabilized. primary/secondary: Maeve (primary), Anil (secondary). coverage note: on-call in eu-zone had delayed alert due to PD escalation policy change.
Anil: ack. saw the alerts come in at ~02:14. was in the middle of a deploy so I didn't pick up until 02:33 when incident-bot paged me.
Maeve: incident-bot timeline — it paged secondary first due to tag mismatch in PD rules. PD log snippet attached to the channel.
incident-bot: [AUTO] PagerDuty: escalation to secondary group at 02:14 UTC, escalation to primary suppressed by filter "service_tag:eu-night=false".
Ruth: can we confirm customer impact list? Ops metrics showed a 12–18% spike in 503s on embed endpoints for eu-west during window. which customers saw errors?
Maeve: preliminary customer-impact: 3 enterprise customers hit ~5–10 failed requests/minute each for ~30 mins; we notified SRE SLA team. no data loss.
Zach: I'll follow up with support to escalate to affected accounts. tagging @support-runbook.
Anil: short notes on mitigation steps I executed: 1) rolled back last routing-rule commit (commit id: 2f9a8c) 2) forced hot-pool failover 3) applied temporary rate-limit to the affected route. commands:
```
# rollback routing rule
kubectl apply -f routing-rules/2026-03-15-prior.yaml
# force failover
redwoodctl failover --pool eu-hot --reason "routing rule rollback"
```
Maeve: after rollback we saw 200s return to baseline within ~3 minutes; p95 error rate decayed by 90% in 10 minutes. p95 latency still +20ms vs baseline, monitoring continuing.
ops-bot: [AUTO] Metric alert cleared: eu-west embeds 503 rate returned to baseline at 02:48 UTC.
Ruth: current status? is there any lingering risk that could re-trigger?
Maeve: current status: stable. root cause hypothesis: a deploy of a routing-rule template introduced a restrictive matcher for pool tags; combined with an unintended PD filter change (service_tag mismatch), primary did not receive initial page so response delayed.
Anil: added an immediate guard: added unit tests for routing-rule matcher matrix and a PD rule smoke test. open tasks list below.
Maeve: next steps (short): 1) Create postmortem ticket (PM-# in progress) 2) Patch PD filter to include fallback escalation 3) Add e2e test in CI for routing rules 4) Runbook update: add a checklist for rollbacks and PD mappings 5) Follow-up - SRE to review hot-pool placement and autoscale thresholds.
Maeve: runbook pointer: https://redwood.local/runbooks/routing-fallbacks (see section "PD-mapping and rollback") — follow that if alerts reappear.
Ruth: please add a concise customer-facing blurb for communications. I can help edit before sending.
Zach: I created support ticket SUP-3218 and notified account owners.
Anil: quick TODOs I'm picking up in the morning: fix PD filter, add CI test, follow up on telemetry gaps.
Maeve: coverage note for the handoff: primary overnight for EU nights remains Maeve, Anil secondary. gap: the PD escalation config allowed suppression of primary for rules without explicit tag; we should not rely on implicit tags. tagging on-call next shift: @Ruth will be primary at 08:00 UTC handover.
Ruth: thanks. I'll take over and monitor dashboards for the next 4 hours, will escalate if we see >2% error rate sustained for 5+ minutes.
Maeve: closing notes: no customer-facing outage declared but degraded experience for subset. PM will own postmortem and RCA. feel free to DM if you want deeper logs. :memo: :white_check_mark:
